summary: Barney Ronay reviews Manchester United's 1-0 home defeat to Bayern Munich, which sealed their bottom-place finish in their Champions League group. He argues United are a muddled squad assembled from the eras of several managers, and that their group-stage record is among the worst by an English club. He also describes the three concurrent jobs of a United manager (managing the past, the present's dysfunction, and everyday metrics), which makes Erik ten Hag's task very hard.
one_line: Ronay's match report on United's 1-0 loss to Bayern, which ended a farcical Champions League campaign and exposed a club stuck in its past.
key_facts: Manchester United lost 1-0 at home to Bayern Munich in their final Champions League group game and finished bottom of the group.
Kingsley Coman scored the only goal just over 10 minutes after Copenhagen scored in the other group game (58 minutes gone), set up by a sneaky round-the-corner pass from Harry Kane.
United conceded 15 goals in the group stage, more than any other English team ever in a Champions League group.
Both group games were goalless at half-time, so United were one goal from reaching the last 16 at that stage.
United's second-half back five was André Onana, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Jonny Evans, Raphaël Varane and Diogo Dalot, signed under Ten Hag, José Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjær and Alex Ferguson.
By the end United had five academy players on the pitch, with ages ranging between 17 and 35.
Group lowlights included Onana diving out of the way of the ball in Munich and in Istanbul, Casemiro's red card, lost leads in Manchester, and Marcus Rashford's red card in Copenhagen.
Ronay compares Bayern's Kimmich-Goretzka-Musiala to United's Amrabat-McTominay-Fernandes, and says Manuel Neuer is what Onana is trying to be; Bayern signed Harry Kane.
Bayern fans sang Football's Coming Home and chanted 'Auf Wiedersehen' at departing United supporters.
United cannot win the league, the Champions League or the Carabao Cup; they still have the FA Cup and a pursuit of fourth or fifth place.
Poor European results this season could damage United's coefficient and keep them out of Europe next season.
Ronay says a United manager must manage the past, the dysfunction of the present (such as a leaking stadium roof), and everyday metrics, all during an unceasing takeover circus.
